### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via requiresConfirmation (symbol, a field of const object TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE), pending_confirmation (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER; a string literal in requiresConfirmation; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via requiresConfirmation (symbol, a field of const object TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE), pending_confirmation (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER; a string literal in requiresConfirmation; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx`  _(via requiresConfirmation (symbol, a field of const object TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via requiresConfirmation (symbol, a field of const object TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via pending_confirmation (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER; a string literal in requiresConfirmation; a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `de4edce9eb915738790e9be880b6283e8f01a67b` — the merge of head `d4ea9c4d3748f9b5ec68369cdf0ea78ad6d15423` into base `162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin de4edce9eb915738790e9be880b6283e8f01a67b && git checkout de4edce9eb915738790e9be880b6283e8f01a67b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf d4ea9c4d3748f9b5ec68369cdf0ea78ad6d15423 && git checkout -B drift-repro 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf && git merge --no-ff d4ea9c4d3748f9b5ec68369cdf0ea78ad6d15423

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- MCP `run_action` / `resume_run` accept-set: `confirm` leaves both closed inputs. Right, and as ruled (6909355256): undeclared on a `.strict()` shape, so `true` and `false`, gated or not, are refused before the handler and the bridge. `tools/list` shows it absent with `additionalProperties: false`.
- The refusal is the existing unknown-key refusal with an exact-key prescription, no new code. Right: `strictUnknownKeyError` gives an exact `guidance` entry precedence over the alias and rename channels (`suggestions.zod.ts`), and no alias on either tool maps to `confirm`.
- The handlers build `request` without the member (not even `undefined`), on the hand-off path and the elicitation path alike. Right. `params.confirm` on an action that declares such a param is untouched.
- `delete_record` / `delete_records` keep the member; the runtime request and the host door (`action-dispatch.ts`, `ai` posture without `confirmationHandOff`) keep reading it. Right, both outside the ruling.
- `@objectstack/spec`: no export, type or schema shape moves; three published texts move (`TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE.requiresConfirmation`, the `ai-service.ts` docblocks, entry 18). The direction is right; two sentences are wrong at this head (S1).
- Served skill and its console mirror drop `confirm?` from both signatures. Right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/console` with `Metadata-protocol: none` matches the rule (a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is on the PR body and the changeset, the BREAKING banner, the FROM/TO lines and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (already-registered …)`) are present, and `Check Changeset` is green. `@objectstack/runtime` moves a test only. For the seat's prose pass: the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet and the PR body's "elicitation is still open on #34318" predate #34318's merge (see S1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on the head: 68, none red. The sharded `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)` is skipped on `pull_request` by its own `if` (`ci.yml`), and the local battery was stopped, so the four edited dogfood files have no reading at any head. The merge queue is their first one; the PR body's "CI's sharded dogfood job is the reading of record" means that run.
- `open_questions`: empty. Acceptance note on #34318: closed, it is in the merge-base and the merged handlers carry no `confirm` read or forward.
- Out-of-scope items the dev report lists as "carrier: none": see S2.
- No earlier contract record on the PR (comment 6915221929 is the claim line). The PR is a draft.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no data access.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts` and entry 18 state the hand-off as the only outcome, which this head contradicts. The guidance says an AI-facing call on a declared-gated action "does not run on that call", that a person confirms "never the agent", and that the two tools answer `pending_confirmation` with the person deciding "in the app". Two doors at this head do otherwise: (a) step 1 of the contract the guidance itself cites (`AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY`) is implemented in the merge-base by #34318, ships from the same unreleased train (`.changeset/33712-…` beside this one, spec still 18.5.0), asks the person in the client and runs the call on `accept`; (b) a host door under the `ai` posture still admits on the member, as this PR's own `ai-service.ts` text and changeset say. Entry 18's `acceptanceCriteria` now reads "any caller gets a pending answer", which its own `replacement` contradicts for an eliciting client, and its header comment says elicitation is added by "a later release". Required: bound the guidance sentence to the two MCP tools and name the in-client step ("in the client when it can be asked, in the app otherwise"); restore the eliciting-client clause in `acceptanceCriteria`; fix the comment. The same omission is in `RETIRED_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER` (`mcp-http-tools.ts`) and the served skill lines; the ruled sentence "confirmation happens in the app, by the person" can stay with the in-client case added beside it.

S2 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/17.tool-requires-confirmation-retired.ts` is a live registry entry whose `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` still prescribe `confirm: true` on the request at "the action door reached from the MCP `run_action` tool". "When it binds" in `ai-service.ts` says the implementing change moves the shipped prescriptions that describe the member; this PR turns that prescription into a call the named tool refuses, and records it as "carrier: none, not filed". Required before landing: amend the entry here, or file the carrier and name it in the Acceptance notes. The same carrier owes `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json`, whose steps send `confirm: true` to `run_action`.

N1 (nit) — `ai-service.ts`: "neither ever accepted-and-ignored it" no longer holds for the runtime request on the MCP bridge path, which takes the member and does not read it (`aiDoorConfirmation` has no request parameter).

N2 (nit) — the ruling's build note asked to rework the `details.confirmationMember` echo; the PR reworks its docblock and keeps the required member on amended refusals from the two tools that refuse it. Accepted deviation: dropping it is a published shape change, and a client that follows the echo meets the loud refusal with its prescription.

The rest holds sentence by sentence against the cited code: the constant keys the refusal; the refusal precedes resolution; the member-gate / amended split of the echo matches `reason`'s own docblock and `confirmationRefusalOf`; entry 18's FROM half matches 18.5.0, where the entry exists and the hand-off does not. The tense pin's required phrases all survive the rewrite. The refusal pins cover both tools, both values, a gated and an ungated action, the bridge-not-called fact and a delete-tool control.
